messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The test case 'testAddNonComparable()' verifies that adding a non-comparable Object to the Frequency instance should raise an IllegalArgumentException. The test calls addValue(new Object()), expecting an exception.

Inspecting the Frequency class, the deprecated addValue(Object v) method simply casts the Object to Comparable<?> and calls addValue(Comparable<?>). This is likely the old API, now deprecated in favor of the type-safe Comparable<?> version.

In the addValue(Comparable<?> v) method, the object is added to an internal freqTable map, but a ClassCastException can be thrown if the new value is not comparable with previous keys in the TreeMap. This is caught and rethrown as an IllegalArgumentException with the message "Value not comparable to existing values."

From the current bug report, the problem is that originally the addValue(Object) was allowed for any Object, but after adding a plain Object first, adding subsequent values fails because the first plain Object is not comparable, and the TreeMap cannot handle mixed types. The report suggests that the addValue(Object) should reject non-comparable objects upfront to prevent this inconsistent state.

Hence, the root cause is that addValue(Object) casts blindly to Comparable<?> without checking and allows a plain Object without comparison capabilities to enter the freqTable, breaking the Frequency. This failed test expects this error condition to throw IllegalArgumentException immediately on adding a non-comparable object, but as the deprecated method internally just casts and calls the Comparable version, it only fails later when trying to add new values.

The addValue(Comparable<?>) method correctly throws IllegalArgumentException when a non-comparable is added inconsistent with previous ones, but the deprecated addValue(Object) lacks a preliminary check on whether the input is Comparable before casting, causing this bug.

Recent bug reports have little relevance to this API issue.

Conclusion: The absence of a type check in addValue(Object) before cast leads to improper acceptance of non-comparable objects and subsequent failures, as the internal map expects comparable keys consistently. The test exposed this by adding a raw Object and expecting an exception, which did not occur at the right time.

Next, I will check if the older addValue(Object) method should have an instanceof Comparable<?> guard before casting.
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Object)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Comparable<?>)
